title: A spectacular view over the Atacama
caption: The Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A man has stepped out of his car somewhere in the Atacama to take in the sky. Above him, the band of the Milky Way rises the full height of the picture, layered with stars and with clouds of gas and dust, and runs roughly toward the centre of our galaxy.

To the right of the frame are the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds. They lie outside the Milky Way: they are separate galaxies in their own right. Up at the top right, the brightest star on show is Canopus, which belongs to the constellation Carina.

ESO describes the scene as giving a real feeling of the cosmic fishbowl we live in. We sit inside a flat disc of stars, looking out along it, and everything in this picture, from the dusty band to the neighbouring galaxies, is seen from that inside position.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects far more light than the eye, so the gas and dust of the Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds appear brighter here than in person.

explore: The photograph was taken somewhere in the Atacama Desert, with no observatory in sight: just a car, a lone figure and the sky. The Milky Way's band is layered with stars and with clouds of gas and dust, stretching roughly toward the heart of our galaxy.
alt: A man beside a car in the desert under the Milky Way, with two faint cloud-like galaxies to the right and a bright star at top right.
